newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish transport firm wants bourse listing in H2.
newsitem.headline: Polish transport firm wants bourse listing in H2.

text.p: Polish transport holding Pekaes Auto-Transport SA plans an initial public offering and wants to enter the Warsaw bourse in the second half of 1997, the spokesman of the company said.
Jerzy Szczesny told Reuters the company was seeking a listing on the main market of the bourse.
"We are preparing an issue prospectus and we want to enter the bourse this year...I think it would be possible in autumn or early winter," he said.
Pekaes Auto-Transport SA, which is 64 percent owned by the state treasury, holds stakes in 14 companies dealing with passenger international transport and goods transport in Poland.
Pekaes Auto-Transport, which employs 3,260, had a net profit of 23.2 million zlotys in 1995 and its revenues amounted to 447 million zlotys.
